title: The Changing Geometry of Grammar: Dimensionality and Neighborhood Reorganization across Transformer Layers
abstract: arXiv:2608.25166v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Transformer representations describe trajectories through high-dimensional vector spaces, which are shaped dynamically as tokens incorporate relational context across layers. Such data tend to concentrate on lower-dimensional sub-manifolds, a form of compression quantified by the Intrinsic Dimensionality (ID), the minimum number of independent variables needed to represent them without significant information loss. In this work, we ask whether the grammatical role of tokens, as marked by their part-of-speech (PoS) tag, shapes the local geometry of this manifold. translated_title: 语法的几何变迁：Transformer层间维度与邻域重组
translated_abstract: 摘要：arXiv:2608.25166v1 公告类型：新 摘要：Transformer表示描述了高维向量空间中的轨迹，这些轨迹随着词元在各层中整合关系上下文而动态形成。此类数据往往集中于较低维的子流形，这是一种通过内在维度（ID）量化的压缩形式，即在不显著丢失信息的情况下表示它们所需的最小独立变量数。在这项工作中，我们探讨词元的语法角色（以其词性（PoS）标记）是否塑造了这一流形的局部几何。为此：（1）我们研究了ID的逐层演化，发现封闭类词比开放类词更早扩展且更早坍缩；（2）我们展示了其扩展和收缩可通过邻域结构的变化来解释，从而反映句子中词间的关系变化；（3）我们比较了编码器（ModernBERT、bigbird-roberta-large）和解码器。
tldr: 本论文发现Transformer中封闭类词的内在维度比开放类词更早扩展和坍缩，并通过邻域结构变化揭示了语法角色如何塑造表示空间的几何演化。
en_tdlr: This paper finds that closed-class words expand and collapse their intrinsic dimensionality earlier than open-class words in Transformers, revealing how grammatical roles shape the geometric evolution of representation space via neighborhood structure changes.
